skill.name: code-review-assistant
skill.description: Review pull requests with coordinated security, performance, style, test, and documentation checks.
skill.summary: Coordinated pull request review with merge readiness feedback and fix suggestions.
skill.author: DNYoussef

security_audit.summary: Most static backtick and /dev/null alerts are Markdown or benign shell redirection false positives. The skill still contains a real Bash automation workflow that runs unpinned npx tools, invokes GitHub CLI actions, and writes generated PR artifacts.

remediation.suggestion: Pin claude-flow versions, use a locked local install, and document package integrity expectations before running review commands.
Default to dry-run or comment-only output, then require explicit user confirmation before gh pr review approves or requests changes.

remediation.issue: Unescaped PR metadata and tool output
remediation.suggestion: Build JSON with jq -n and --arg values, and sanitize Markdown before posting generated PR comments.
Move complex shell logic into a reviewed script with argument validation, quoted variables, and small documented commands.

semantic_findings.title: Unpinned Remote Tool Execution
semantic_findings.description: The workflow repeatedly invokes npx claude-flow without a pinned version or local integrity controls. A changed package could run third-party code during review.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The lines directly call npx claude-flow subcommands from the shell workflow. No pinned version, checksum, or local lockfile is shown in the skill.

semantic_findings.title: Automated GitHub Review State Changes
semantic_findings.description: The workflow posts PR comments and can approve or request changes based on generated scores. This can alter repository review state without a human confirmation step.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The GitHub CLI commands are explicit and include gh pr comment plus gh pr review with approve and request-changes actions. The workflow does not show an approval gate before running them.

semantic_findings.title: Unescaped PR Metadata in Generated Artifacts
semantic_findings.description: The workflow interpolates PR titles and generated tool output into JSON and Markdown here-docs. Malicious PR metadata can corrupt artifacts or inject misleading review content.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The script assigns PR metadata and embeds variables and command output directly into generated JSON and Markdown. The skill does not show JSON escaping or Markdown sanitization.

content.user_title: Review Pull Requests with Multi-Agent Checks
content.value_statement: Manual PR review can miss security, test, and quality issues. This skill coordinates specialized checks and prepares merge feedback for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code workflows.
actual_capabilities: Gather PR metadata and changed file paths through GitHub CLI.
Run security, performance, style, test, and documentation review checks.
Aggregate review outputs into a merged score and category summary.
Generate fix suggestions from collected review findings using Codex.
Post a PR review comment and approve or request changes.
limitations: Requires authenticated GitHub CLI and repository review permissions.
Depends on claude-flow and Codex CLI behavior in the local environment.
Does not fully escape all PR metadata before writing generated artifacts.
Can alter PR review state, so supervised execution is recommended.

use_cases.title: Pre-Merge Repository Review
use_cases.description: Run a broad PR quality check before maintainers decide whether a change is ready to merge.

use_cases.title: Focused Security Pass
use_cases.description: Review changed files for unsafe patterns, secrets, and critical security blockers before approval.

use_cases.title: Release Readiness Audit
use_cases.description: Combine quality, test, and documentation signals into a merge readiness summary for release branches.

prompt_templates.title: Review One Pull Request
prompt_templates.prompt: Review pull request 123 with all default checks. Summarize blockers, warnings, suggestions, and merge readiness.

prompt_templates.title: Focus on Security and Tests
prompt_templates.prompt: Review pull request 123 with focus areas security and tests. Prioritize issues that should block merge.

prompt_templates.title: Prepare Fix Suggestions
prompt_templates.prompt: Review pull request 123 and generate fix suggestions for each confirmed issue. Group suggestions by severity and file area.

prompt_templates.title: Run a Supervised Quality Gate
prompt_templates.prompt: Review pull request 123 for release readiness. Do not approve or request changes until I confirm the final decision.

output_examples.input: Review PR 123 with all checks enabled.
output_examples.output: Overall score 84. Merge ready with warnings. Security passed, tests need one coverage improvement, and documentation needs release notes.

output_examples.input: Review PR 123 with security focus only.
output_examples.output: Security review found one blocking secret-handling issue and two medium validation concerns. Request changes until the blocker is fixed.

output_examples.input: Generate fix suggestions for review findings.
output_examples.output: Suggested fixes include adding input validation, improving boundary tests, and updating the API usage notes before approval.

best_practices: Run the skill from a clean working tree with an authenticated GitHub CLI session.
Use comment-only or dry-run behavior when testing it on active repositories.
Confirm generated findings before approving or requesting changes on protected branches.
anti_patterns: Running the workflow on untrusted repositories with broad GitHub tokens.
Letting automated approvals replace required human review for sensitive changes.
Treating generated scores as final proof that a pull request is safe.

faq.question: Does this skill need GitHub access?
faq.answer: Yes. It uses GitHub CLI commands and needs repository permissions for viewing PRs and posting review feedback.

faq.question: Can it approve a pull request?
faq.answer: Yes. The documented workflow can approve or request changes, so use it with supervised permissions.

faq.question: Does it write files locally?
faq.answer: Yes. It creates a PR review directory and stores intermediate review artifacts there.

faq.question: Can it generate fixes automatically?
faq.answer: It can generate fix suggestions from review findings, but developers should inspect them before applying changes.

faq.question: Is it limited to security review?
faq.answer: No. It also covers performance, style, tests, documentation, and overall quality scoring.

faq.question: Should it run on protected branches?
faq.answer: Use dry-run behavior first, then require human confirmation before any review state changes.
